messages.subject: Warnings of INVALID MODEL FITTED
parts:
Hi everyone, my name is Dayron and I am looking at old material to see whether it should be analyzed or not through Distance Sampling or how to better design the survey in the future. the data are divided in two strata and so in one of these strata (stratum A) there are very few detections, but I want to try to fit a curve anyway. 

In the Log I see that there are three warnings which say:"Maximum probability of detection is greater than one:invalid model fitted", but despite these seemingly big mistakes, no Errors (so analysis not run) are signaled..why? Why if the model fitted is not valid I do get results anyway (which are even more statistically significant than those of other analyses which are valid)? 

I think that it has to do with the stratum A, because with the stratum B everything seems to be ok. As regards stratum A effectively I can see both very strangely high numbers on the y axis of the detection function and a strangely low value of the resulting estimated density; but the Q-Q plot seems very good and even the probability of a greater Chi-squared value. 
How should I interpret these results? What about the warnings without Errors? 

Thanks a lot for your time

(I attach here some screenshots hoping to make you understand the situation better than I explained)

Have a good and safe day

Dayron

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Warnings of INVALID MODEL FITTED
parts:
Dayron

Yes, the Distance software cannot always save you from yourself.  You were suspicious of the data from Stratum A, and those suspicions were warranted.  Having only 14 detections is the first indication that results will not be reliable.  With none of those detections being within 30m(?) of the transect, you know you will not be abl to fit a deetection function with detection probability starting at 1 on the transect and declining thereafter.

Distance is following its instruction, namely trying to place a detection function throough the data you observed.  It has done that reasonably well, but in doing so, it has produced a ridiculous result, an estimate of detection probability of >20000 (rather than <1).

This reinforces the concept that you cannot simply take the results from Distance output and place them directly into your reports.  It also makes plain that you investigate not only errors, but warnings as well.

How should you interpret these results?  You cannot expect reasonable detection function fits to data that a) don't appear to conform to the assumption that detectability on the transect is perfect and decreases as a function of perpendicular distance and b) that consists of a small number of detections.

Eric Rexstad
Centre for Research into Ecological and Environmental Modelling
University of St Andrews
St Andrews KY16 9LZ

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Warnings of INVALID MODEL FITTED
parts:
Eric 
Thanks a lot for your clarification, you just confirmed my thoughts. Unfortunately for that stratum there were too few detections and all the animals were recorded at some distance from the transects. Maybe some of them moved as a consequence of the presence of the observer but there is no way to know. If we had much time probably more detections would have occurred close to the line.
I thought it would have been wrong not to try a stratified approach, but now I know it would be better to try again just with all the observations together. In the other stratum I have 51 detections and a reasonable histogram,so I'll try this. 

Thank you and good evening/day to everyone

Dayron
